newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHIPPING CO NEEDS TO IMPROVE MANAGEMENT - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: SHIPPING CO NEEDS TO IMPROVE MANAGEMENT - REPORT.

text.p: One of Latvia's largest companies, Latvian Shipping Company, said it needs to improve its financial management in 1997, especially in its holding companies, the company told newspaper Dienas Bizness on Thursday.
From August 1997, its holding companies will face monthly financial reporting requirements, chairman Druvis Skulte told the newspaper.
Lack of proper financial management was a reason the group made losses in 1996 and dividends from the holding companies were not returning to the mother company, Skulte added.
Skulte said he saw tanker transport as its priority and its board has decided radically to change its policy in the dry-cargo transports.
"Continuing in the dry-cargo market with existing ships and organisation would mean only losses," Skulte said.
The group could return to the dry-cargo market if tanker transports faced a sharp fall in business but to compete the company would need new ships.

Skulte said that the debts of the company also have to be settled before privatisation. He said that the debts to energy group Latvenergo should be capitalised by turning them into shares in Latvenergo.
